page.layout: Single column of verse, with a running head above and a page number at top left. Under the text: a right-aligned line "I. I. B.", then an ornament (no text), and at the lower right the catchword "IN".

main_text.head: ALIVD.
main_text.p: Illa dies terris quæ te tulit ante, Navarre, Ut columen patriæ conspicerétve patrem, Indignata tibi crudelia fata parare Guisiadem, hunc subito frigore iusta ferit, Unius ardentes restinguens sanguine flammas, Gallorum[?] una plurima bella nece. Clara dies tanti regis natalibus, Euge Clarior adscito funere Guisiadæ.
main_text.head: ALIVD.
main_text.p: Quæ te (Rex) terris ostendit prima, Navarre Signetur creta nobiliore dies Nascentis nam fausta prius cunabula vitæ Quum dedit, hoc dixit non satis esse tibi, Ni te perpetuo comitetur amica fuore[?], Atq; hostes[?] cunctos perdat acerba tuos. Hoc facit, unius lethæo flumine mersum Guisiadis tandem quum rapit illa caput.

page.notes: Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. Printed "Vt", "Vnius", "Vna", "vnius" are given as Ut, Unius, una, unius by the u/v rule. Doubtful: "Gallorum" is followed by a mark resembling a superscript g or a stroked sign, not clearly readable; "fuore" is uncertain (possibly furore); "hostes" has a damaged join before "cunctos". The ornament at the foot carries no text. The verse is set as stanzas with lines run together into one paragraph each.
